structured_output.summary:
Root cause: three places identify a typed-locator @reference solely by its locator string (`at_reference`), with no owner scoping. When two independently controlled consumers (different `source_concept_id`) reference the same target with the same locator, they collide: (1) projection.py's ADD reducer drops the second consumer's materialized reference outright (dedup key = locator only); (2) consensus_invalidation.active_references_to() removed_refs is keyed by locator only, so one owner removing their reference silently un-lists the other owner's still-active one, and plan_aux_events() emits aux events whose after_state carries no owner, so the projection's AUTO_UPDATED/TARGET_SUPERSEDED matcher (also locator-only) applies one owner's response to both; (3) concept_retire_gate._collect_batch_migrations records batch-removed reference ids by locator only, so one owner's AtReferenceRemoved is accepted as migration evidence for another owner's still-active blocking reference. The projection's REMOVED branch additionally never matched typed-locator removals at all (it only checked the endpoint-shaped `reference_id` field), which independently breaks per-owner remove/replay for that shape.

Fix: key/match typed-locator lifecycle events by (locator, source_concept_id) instead of locator alone, in all three places, with a documented graceful degrade to the old locator-only match whenever the incoming event/payload carries no owner field at all (`source_concept_id`/owner is `None`) — this keeps already-committed pre-fix history replaying exactly as before (idempotent, no legacy-data breakage) while new events get correct cross-owner isolation going forward. Also extend the projection REMOVED branch to actually recognize the typed-locator shape (mirroring the fields ADD already uses), since without it a typed reference could never be deactivated.
